correctness.rationale: For even shore size the explicit threshold response yields complete closed-form recurrent-state and two-cycle counts and F^3=F. For odd size the fixed-point count follows by four critical one-count cases. An exact Fourier–Motzkin certificate covers all odd sizes: 30 feasible five-step threshold branches agree at steps three and five, and 608 nonfixed two-step candidate systems have only two feasible extreme cases, giving one primitive two-cycle. This is rational elimination on a superset of all allowed integer multiplicities, so it is an all-size proof. Independent vertex-level exhaustive tests for shore sizes 3..8 confirm every formula and bound. Entry-time witnesses establish sharpness.

value.rationale: The exact arithmetic parity bifurcation on a natural connected network yields one primitive two-cycle for every odd shore size but (binomial(n,n/2)+2)(binomial(n,n/2)+1)/2 for even sizes, asymptotically 4^n/(pi n). It supplies complete recurrent configurations, fixed counts, and sharp size-dependent convergence times. A generic threshold period-two theorem does not predict the size of the recurrent set, and the matching deletion creates a structurally motivated critical-scale regime.
